issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem 3.1 (ae-DMCE), several critical mathematical steps fail: (1) In Step 2, bounding E[|S_{y,i} - U_{t_i}^m|^2] in (3.12) produces an O(1) constant C(1+h) that does not vanish with h. In (3.13), this non-vanishing term is dropped without justification; retaining it in (3.8), where it is multiplied by 1/h and summed over N steps, produces an error of order O(1/h^2), causing the bound to diverge as h -> 0. (2) In Step 4, E[|S_{z,i} - V_{t_i}^m|^2] in (3.19) is bounded by CN because the Monte Carlo average was replaced by a single path. In (3.16), this term is multiplied by 2h, yielding an O(1) constant 2CT that is silently omitted in (3.21); summing it over N steps in (3.22) yields an O(N) = O(1/h) divergence. (3) In (3.10) and (3.18), the authors assert E[|Y_i - S_{y,i}|^2] = E[|R_{i,2}^y|^2] and E[|Z_i - S_{z,i}|^2] = E[|R_{i,2}^z|^2]; however, S_{y,i} and S_{z,i} are defined via the neural networks NN_{y,i+1} and NN_{z,i}, whereas R_{i,2}^y and R_{i,2}^z are defined in (3.5b) using the simulated Euler paths Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m} and Z_i^{\pi,m}. These objects are distinct, so the identities do not hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must correctly preserve the Monte Carlo variance reduction factor 1/K_i in S_{y,i} and S_{z,i}, bound the local conditional variances by O(h) rather than O(1) or O(N), correctly propagate the regression errors of the network targets S_{y,i} and S_{z,i} through the backward induction without deleting non-vanishing terms, and re-establish the convergence rates in Theorem 3.2.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.1 (ae-DMCE) is unproved and its claimed upper error bound is mathematically invalid. Consequently, Theorem 3.2 (thm:added-1), which directly relies on Theorem 3.1 to establish half-order convergence under GroupSort networks, is also invalidated.
issues.title: Fatal omissions of diverging terms and invalid residual identification in error analysis of DBR scheme
issues.why_classification: The error bound of Theorem 3.1 and the convergence rate of Theorem 3.2 constitute the core theoretical foundations of the paper. Repairing them requires substantially rebuilding the error propagation and regression analysis architecture, as the current proof drops terms that diverge as O(1/h^2) and O(1/h).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The error estimate for the $Z$-component can be derived using the same arguments as in Steps 3 and 4 of the proof of Theorem \ref{ae-DMCE}; thus, the details are omitted here.

issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 4.3 (ae-DMCE-R) and its proof: (1) The induction inequality in (4.8) fails to close. The LHS bounds |\bar{Y}_i^{\pi,m} - \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_i|^2 (unreflected Euler step vs reflected network), whereas the RHS contains |Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m} - \widehat{\mathcal{NN}}_{y,i+1}|^2 (reflected Euler variable vs unreflected network). Because \widehat{\mathcal{NN}}_{y,i+1} is unreflected while Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m} is projected by max{., g}, |Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m} - \widehat{\mathcal{NN}}_{y,i+1}| cannot be controlled by |Y_{i+1}^{\pi,m} - \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_{i+1}|. (2) Equation (4.8) contains the term CN * E[|\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_i - \bar{\mathcal{U}}_{t_i}^m|^2]. Equation (4.9) already bounds E[|\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_i - \bar{\mathcal{U}}_{t_i}^m|^2] by C * (N |\widehat{R}_{i+1}^y|^2 + |\widehat{R}_i^z|^2). Substituting (4.9) into (4.8) produces terms of order N^2 |\widehat{R}^y|^2 and N |\widehat{R}^z|^2, which when summed over N time steps yield N^3 |\widehat{R}^y|^2 and N^2 |\widehat{R}^z|^2; however, (4.10) and the theorem statement discard an entire factor of N. (3) In (4.11), combining (4.10) with (4.3) omits the discretization error \varepsilon(h) entirely from the displayed bound. (4) The proof omits the Z-component by referring to Steps 3 and 4 of Theorem 3.1, which contain fatal divergences.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reformulate the induction using non-expansive properties of the obstacle projection on compatible reflected quantities, resolve the order-of-magnitude discrepancy in the factor of N, retain the discretization error \varepsilon(h) in the final bound, and provide a valid proof for the Z-component.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 4.3 (ae-DMCE-R) is mathematically invalid; the error bound claimed for the reflected DBR scheme applied to variational inequalities is unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid induction step and order-of-magnitude inconsistency in error analysis for variational inequalities
issues.why_classification: Theorem 4.3 is the only theoretical convergence result for the variational inequality extension. Resolving the induction mismatch and the inconsistent powers of N requires constructing an entirely new proof argument for the reflected BSDE setting.
